description: The bellboy's sleepwalking-like guidance and unresponsive, eerie behavior alert the investigators, the threat of vampires looming.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "You really should hear his story."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Hello Ms. Cavallaro, I'm player4, currently a medical student at Miskatonic University."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "A man of indomitable spirit, a respectable adventurer."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Yes, ma'am, my name is player12. But I couldn't have made it this far without the help of these friends."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: After listening to each introduction, Caterina's eyes grew wider and wider, finally unable to resist clapping in admiration: What a fantastic group! She first playfully tilted her head at player2: A psychology top student from Miskatonic University? It seems I have to watch what I say~ Turning to player4, she made a praying gesture: Medical students are the greatest! When I sprained my ankle during a performance last time, I was saved by a doctor just like you. Hearing Professor Bailan's identity as an archaeology professor, she nearly knocked over her wine glass in excitement: My goodness! I've collected so many ancient Roman coins, I must consult you another day! Finally, she looked gently at Johnson and said: Mr. Johnson, your story reminds me of the poet Rodolfo from La Bohème! Adventures in Paris must be more thrilling than any opera. She raised her refilled glass: A toast to meeting such charming travel companions! It seems this Orient Express journey is destined to become a legend!

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "You flatter me, but still," #raises glass "a toast to our unexpected meeting and to good health!"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Cheers, cheers.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Yes, yes, let's celebrate today's safety." #Raises glass.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Everyone chatted happily with Caterina, and before they knew it, it was 11 PM. Caterina stood up slightly tipsy, her steps a bit unsteady, and playfully winked: Wait a moment, I'll be right back~ About 15 minutes later, she returned to the salon car with light steps, completely transformed—wearing a dazzling silver-white gown, mascara outlining deep eyeliner, a Life Cross necklace shining brilliantly around her neck under the light. Dear friends, she curtsied gracefully, allow me to perform for you the aria I will sing in Milan three days later. The people present immediately responded with enthusiastic applause, a few attendants couldn't help but stop to watch, and the salon car instantly became a small opera house.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Sits up straight, alert.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: #Finds a suitable spot to stand and listen to her singing voice.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Listens attentively, having some understanding of music after all, since a certain maid sings by his ear every day.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Caterina clasped her hands over her chest, her gaze becoming gentle and distant: This song has special meaning for me. When I was five, my grandmother first took me to La Scala to see Aida, and that night completely changed my life. She chuckled lightly, before that night I was full of thoughts about wanting a little pony, but when the curtain rose and the music started, I knew—I wanted to be the one standing on that stage. She stroked the Life Cross necklace on her chest, my grandmother said, sing your wishes with an aria, and one day they will come true. So... She took a deep breath, straightened up, now I will sing "Triumphant Return," this is the moment of Aida's greatest inner struggle, her beloved Radamès and her father Amonasro belong to the opposing sides of Egypt and Ethiopia...

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Out of politeness, acts quite excited.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Her singing suddenly rang out, clear as spring water striking stone. The high notes were like silver bells trembling, the low murmurs like silk rubbing. Every turn of phrase accurately outlined Aida's painful struggle—loyalty to her lover and duty to her homeland tore and blended in her voice. When she sang "my tears will flood the Nile," a few attendants unconsciously held their breath; and the lingering final note of "but my heart will always belong to you" made player4 instinctively grip the arm of the sofa. While singing, she constantly lightly stroked the cross on her necklace, as if performing a sacred ritual. After the last long note gradually faded, the car was so quiet you could hear the champagne bubbles popping, everyone still immersed in that ancient love story woven by song.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Bravo!" #Cheers.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Snaps out of the awe, then applauds.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Leaning to the side, expression seems slightly dazed, an exceptionally familiar feeling, making even a professor like him sigh with emotion, a smile curling at the corner of his mouth.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Applauds, vigorously.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Caterina took an elegant bow amidst the prolonged applause, her cheeks flushed with excitement. She walked up to the investigators and said: The tickets I gave you earlier are front-row seats for the night of the 16th, as a thank you for being my best audience tonight~ She winked slyly, remember the hotel at the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II I promised? It's all arranged! Giving a small yawn, she waved her sequined gloves: See you tomorrow, dear friends! Her silver gown rustled as she fluttered away like a wisp of starlight, leaving only a faint scent of jasmine perfume in the air. You take out your tickets, which read: La Scala Opera House · January 16th · Aida Premiere · VIP Seats.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Truly worthy of a big star."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The lights in the salon car dimmed slightly, and the merry crowd gradually dispersed. A few passengers whose spirits were still high gathered around the card table in the corner, coins clinking on the green felt. The rhythmic swaying of the train made the ice cubes in the champagne glasses gently collide. Occasional scattered lights flashed by outside the window, quickly swallowed by darkness again.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Haa~~ Time for bed, see you all tomorrow." #Johnson bids everyone farewell and goes back to his room to sleep.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The night-running Orient Express, like a moving castle, carrying countless secrets and stories, traverses through the peaks of the Alps.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Sleep time."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Goes to sleep, attempting to practice cat language in dreams.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Well, what a wonderful night." #Drinks the last of the fine wine in his glass, raises the empty cup towards the south, as if toasting someone from afar.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Drinks a little wine before bed, ushering in quality sleep.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The investigators slept exceptionally soundly this night, even their dreams tinged with the splendor of the opera.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: As the morning sun filtered through the gaps in the curtains, the attendant gently knocked and delivered hot coffee and croissants. Just as they were enjoying their breakfast spread with jam, the train gradually slowed down, and the scenery of Milan's suburbs began to appear outside the window. The attendant politely knocked to remind them: Gentlemen, we are about to arrive at Milan station, please prepare to disembark.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Great, we arrived just as we woke up."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Ten minutes later, you faintly heard the cries of newspaper boys and the whistles of steam locomotives outside the window. The Orient Express let out one final long sigh and came to a steady stop beside the platform.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Ah! How did everyone rest? It seems we have already reached our destination."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We're here, we can get off now."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The investigators had just stepped out of the carriage when they saw Caterina standing alone at the edge of the platform. Her agent was not far away, instructing a taxi driver about the destination. Suddenly, a black Alfa Romeo sports car sped over and screeched to a halt right in front of Caterina. The door flung open, two hands reached out from inside, and yanked her into the car. The whole process was too fast to react to—the door slammed shut, the sports car's engine roared as it accelerated, and in the blink of an eye, it disappeared into the morning mist at the end of the platform, leaving only a few wisps of gasoline-scented smoke. The agent's briefcase fell to the ground with a thud, papers scattering everywhere. He stood frozen in place, his face pale.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Not accurate, to be precise, it's treating player4 like a cat to pet."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The agent then shuddered as if waking from a dream and stammered in reply: O-of course not! We arranged for an ordinary taxi... He suddenly grabbed player2's sleeve, his fingers trembling: Good heavens, who were those people? Where did they take Caterina? In the morning mist on the platform, a few passengers began to cast curious glances their way, while the black sports car was long gone in the distance.

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "That's stating the obvious, she was kidnapped."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Daring to kidnap a big star in public, feels like the forces behind it aren't simple."

conversation.speaker: player12

conversation.speaker: player2

conversation.text: "Chase?"

He frantically rummaged through the documents in his pocket, papers scattering everywhere. She even said she'd perform at the Fascist party's charity gala these past two days... Those Blackshirt boys clearly all liked her...

Last week, the actress Marta in Rome went missing... Her agent also went to the Carabinieri, and three days later people found his right hand... in the Tiber River."

conversation.speaker: player3

Her only enemy might be that tenor at La Scala who always sends her white roses—because he kept singing off-key, she suggested he change careers and sell sausages..."

The front page is fantastic—photos of the Fascist volunteer parade are bigger than the football news! He proudly shakes open the newspaper.

conversation.text: The agent shook his head vigorously, the fat under his chin trembling: Mother of God, her family are the most law-abiding spice merchants in Bologna! Her father died ten years ago, her mother still runs a small grocery on Via della Chiesa di San Luca."

conversation.speaker: player2

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The ink smell is still fresh. The front page prominently features a photo of Mussolini inspecting a newly built orphanage, with the headline "Leader Promises to Solve Southern Famine." The second page carries a preview of the La Scala Opera House's spring season, with Caterina's name listed third on the program. Flipping to the society section reveals only ordinary news: the local chamber of commerce is holding a charity sale, and the University of Milan's archaeology department has received a new donation. The classified ads section prints promotional information for cafes, shoe repair shops, and bookstores, with nothing unusual. The most urgent matter the entire newspaper suggests is probably the weather forecast predicting possible rain over the weekend.

In the distance, an accordion plays a cheerful tarantella, but the notes drifting from the bellows are always half a beat slower than they should be.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "No, I mean the people here."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Milan, Italy's most prosperous city, presents a suffocatingly contradictory scene in winter. While the bricks and cement are solid and trustworthy, the flesh and blood are not. Milan is neither reckless nor lively. It feels like a city gradually fading into gray. Under the magnificent skyline of Gothic spires and Renaissance arcades, the streets are neat to the point of rigidity. Shop windows display the most fashionable goods in all of Europe, yet no one stops to admire them. The Milanese seem afflicted by a kind of depression, as if they have finally, months after a close relative's death, received the belated blow of realizing the person is truly gone.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I'm starting to miss France, though I really don't want to ride old Henry's carriage again."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "It looks like their vitality has been eaten away."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Cheer up. Feeling sad here won't bring your big star back."

conversation.speaker: player5

But for God's sake... in public, please call me Mr. Rossi... His voice suddenly catches because he sees a young man in a black shirt nearby roughly stuffing a workers' newspaper into a trash can, his movements violent as if burying a corpse. The agent immediately shrinks his neck.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Alright, I'll call you Cicero then."

conversation.speaker: player3

Professor Bailan noticed his fear reaction was very genuine and pure—dilated pupils, rapid breathing, uncontrollably trembling fingers—completely like an ordinary person terrified by a sudden kidnapping, with no signs of performance or concealment.

After saying this, he continues trimming his nails as if nothing had happened.
